brand.name: Pinoy Pages
brand.mirrorNote: Your page on Pinoy Pages is the product, and the web page is included at no extra charge. Your QR connects your own cards, flyers, signs and counter card to that page.
brand.reportNote: Scan counts reported monthly for every Verified listing. No results are guaranteed.
brand.printNote: The printed edition is a short-run proof copy: one copy for each Verified listing, plus sales copies. It is not sold or handed out to the public.
brand.annualNote: Pilot Edition (magazine + directory). Prices are per issue. The website is updated year-round.
brand.eventNote: Official deadlines come from Canada Revenue Agency pages. 2027 dates follow CRA's published rules; confirm each on canada.ca when CRA posts its 2027 list.
brand.pitch: Get your business in Pinoy Pages 2026–2027 — online all year, with a QR code that brings customers to your verified page.
brand.productNote: The website is the product. Print is the proof copy.
brand.validity: Released spring (April 16, 2027) and valid through summer and fall until the next edition.
brand.badgeRule: Payment never buys the badge. Verified makes a business eligible for Verified Kabayan; the badge is earned by four checks: a ~15-minute visit (kabayan-owned or run, really trading, ZCard completed) plus one mutual vouch from a verified business. Pilot: founding members are vouched for at the visit.
brand.qrLine: Check the preview says pinoypages.ca before you tap.
brand.bridgeRule: This page never asks for a login, a payment or personal information. Only “Save contact” and “Call”. If a page that looks like ours asks for more, do not enter anything and report it.
keepRules: One year at a time: the badge is valid for one edition. A light re-check at renewal updates “Verified [date]”.
A vouch stays active: keep at least one mutual vouch. If it's removed, you have 60 days to replace it.
Details stay current: keep your phone and ZCard up to date. A dead phone or a closed business pauses the badge.
Renew to keep it: no renewal, no badge. The listing drops to Free.
Complaints are reviewed: a complaint pauses the badge while we review it.
brand.adsNote: Ads return in the April 2027 edition.

ads.headline: SAMPLE AD — Tax season made easy
ads.body: Personal and self-employed returns in English and Tagalog. This is a sample ad to show how a sold full page appears online.

ads.headline: SAMPLE AD — Your books, done monthly
ads.body: Bookkeeping, payroll and HST filing for small businesses. This is a sample half-page ad.

listings.name: Bituin Tax & Bookkeeping
listings.hours: Mon–Fri 10am–7pm · Sat 10am–3pm · Sundays in March and April
listings.serviceArea: Scarborough, Markham and Pickering. Home visits for seniors in Malvern.
listings.story: Maria Santos did her first returns at her dining table on Sheppard Avenue, for nurses from her building who kept getting letters from CRA they couldn't read. Twelve years later the table is an office in a plaza near Malvern, and the nurses send their kids. She still keeps a box of Kleenex on the desk in April.
listings.quote: Most people who come in are not bad with money. They're just scared of the envelope.
listings.why: She explains your notice of assessment in Tagalog, line by line, before you sign anything.

listings.name: Araw CPA Professional Corp.
listings.story: A two-partner CPA office above a bakery on Dundas Street West. Mostly small corporations, a few families who followed them from a bigger firm.
listings.why: Corporate and personal returns under one roof.

listings.name: Malaya Community Tax Clinic
listings.serviceArea: North York, near Bathurst and Wilson
listings.story: Volunteers from a parish group run free tax nights in a church basement every February. Bring your slips and a pen.
listings.why: Free, and they speak Ilocano.

listings.name: Dagat Tax Services
listings.tagline: Newcomer & family returns, benefits and RRSP questions
listings.story: Ramon dela Cruz came over as a caregiver's husband and spent his first winter shovelling driveways in Meadowvale. He learned taxes because nobody could explain to his wife why her benefit stopped. Now most of his clients arrived in the last three years, and a lot of them are from Cebu, like him.
listings.quote: The first return is the one that sets up everything else. Benefits, credit, all of it. So we take our time.
listings.why: He's patient with first-timers and answers in Bisaya if that's easier for you.

listings.name: Sinag Accounting
listings.tagline: Small-business books, HST and year-end for sole proprietors
listings.serviceArea: Scarborough and East York. Video calls for clients outside Toronto.
listings.story: Joy Fernandez worked in a bank back home in Dagupan and does the books the same way: neatly, early and with a printout you can keep. Her clients are mostly sole proprietors. Cleaners, PSWs with side clients, a few food sellers from the weekend markets on Lawrence.
listings.quote: If you start a side business in June, come see me in June. Not the next April.
listings.why: She tells you in plain words whether you need to register for HST yet.

listings.name: Bagong Bayan Tax Desk
listings.tagline: Seasonal tax desk for families and seniors
listings.story: A seasonal desk that a retired bookkeeper, Nestor Ramos, opens every spring in a community room off Queen Street East. He hasn't renewed for this edition yet, so his badge has lapsed.
listings.quote: Same chair, same calculator, every spring.
listings.why: Evening hours in tax season, good for shift workers.

listings.name: Hiraya Insurance & Mortgage
listings.tagline: Life, home & auto cover for Filipino families
listings.serviceArea: Etobicoke, Mississauga and the west end
listings.story: Liza Reyes sold her first policy to her aunt, who made her explain it three times at a christening party. She still explains things three times. Her office is a small unit near Islington and Dixon, with a rice cooker in the back and a framed photo of that aunt on the wall.
listings.quote: Insurance is a promise. I don't want you to buy one you don't understand.
listings.why: No pressure to buy the same day. She sends a one-page summary in Tagalog you can show your family.

listings.name: Kalayaan Financial Planning
listings.story: A one-person planning practice that mostly meets clients after church on Sundays.
listings.why: Weekend appointments.

listings.name: Tala Life & Auto Insurance
listings.tagline: Life, home & auto cover for Filipino families
listings.story: Jun Bautista has sold auto and life policies on Kipling Avenue for nine years. A customer complaint is under review, so the badge is paused until the review is done.
listings.quote: Call me before you renew. Every year.
listings.why: Long hours on Saturdays.

listings.name: Luzon Mortgage Desk
listings.tagline: Mortgage renewals and first homes, explained in plain English or Tagalog
listings.story: Carmela Aquino was verified for last year's edition and hasn't booked her re-check yet, so her badge shows as expired. Her listing stays up.
listings.quote: Read the renewal letter the day it arrives.
listings.why: Renewal letters explained in English or Tagalog.

listings.name: Tahanan Mortgage Partners
listings.tagline: First homes, FHSA questions and renewals
listings.story: Ben Ocampo's parents rented the same basement off Steeles for eleven years. He became a mortgage agent partly to find out why nobody had ever sat them down. Most of his meetings now happen at a kitchen table, with a grandmother listening from the sofa.
listings.quote: Honestly, the hard part isn't the mortgage. It's the first two years of saving. That's where I help.
listings.why: He'll meet the whole family, including the grandparent who's putting money in.

listings.name: Padayon Financial Planning
listings.tagline: Plain-language planning for OFW families now settled in Canada
listings.serviceArea: Mississauga and Etobicoke. Video calls anywhere in Ontario.
listings.story: Rosa Mabini worked in Hong Kong for six years before Canada, and she still thinks like an OFW: send, save, protect. She opened her practice off Hurontario after helping three families from her church sort out policies they'd bought back home and never looked at again.
listings.quote: A lot of us have a policy in the Philippines and one here and no idea if they overlap.
listings.why: She reviews the policies you already have before suggesting anything new.

listings.name: Perlas Bookkeeping & Payroll
listings.tagline: Bookkeeping, payroll & HST filing for small business
listings.story: Grace Villanueva keeps the books for a Filipino eatery, two cleaning companies and a dental office, and she knows which of them pays on time. She started in a shared office on Denison Street with one client, her cousin's catering business, and a shoebox of receipts.
listings.quote: Bring me the shoebox. I've seen worse. I'll show you how to never need a shoebox again.
listings.why: Fixed monthly price, and she answers texts on Thursday nights.

listings.name: Mabuhay Payroll Services
listings.story: A small payroll service on the Danforth for businesses with under twenty staff.
listings.why: Simple payroll for small teams.

listings.name: Sampaguita Business Registry
listings.tagline: Register your business, get your HST number, start right
listings.story: Paolo Mendoza used to work the counter at a registration office, and he got tired of watching people pay twice for the same form. His own office is near Weston Road and Highway 7. Many of his clients are family businesses, a roast-pork catering line or a car-detailing van, that have run informally for years.
listings.quote: You don't have to be big to be registered. You just have to be real.
listings.why: He tells you which registration you actually need, and which you don't yet.

listings.name: Habi Payroll & HR
listings.tagline: Payroll, ROEs and simple HR paperwork for small employers
listings.story: Annabelle Santiago did HR for a hotel near the airport for years, and she still starts her day at 8 sharp. Her clients are small employers: a bakery with six staff, a home care agency, a trucking company run by two brothers from Iloilo.
listings.quote: When someone leaves, the ROE should go out that week. People are waiting on it for EI.
listings.why: Fast Records of Employment, so your staff aren't left waiting.

listings.name: Kawayan Corporate Filings
listings.story: Edwin Torres handles annual returns and minute books for small corporations. His listed phone number hasn't answered at two check calls, so the badge is paused until a re-check.
listings.quote: Your minute book should not live in a plastic bag.
listings.why: Keeps small corporations' paperwork in order.

listings.name: Ligaya Creative Studio
listings.tagline: Logos, menus and flyers for Filipino-owned businesses
listings.story: Andrea Lim designs menus and flyers from a studio in Parkdale. She signed up for Verified and her visit is booked, so there's no badge yet.
listings.quote: Your menu is your first ad.
listings.why: Designs that print well at the corner print shop.

listings.name: Bayanihan Notary & Translation
listings.story: Weekend translation and commissioning for documents going to or coming from the Philippines.
listings.why: Open on weekends.

listings.name: Ilaw Virtual Assistants
listings.story: Two sisters who do invoicing and scheduling for small offices, fully online.
listings.why: Affordable admin help.

listings.name: Kidlat IT Support
listings.tagline: Laptops, Wi-Fi and POS help for small offices
listings.story: Mark Garcia fixes the things that stop a small office cold: the printer before a payroll run, the card machine on a Saturday at the bakery. He started out repairing laptops for friends in his parents' garage off Yonge Street and never really stopped.
listings.quote: If your card machine dies at 11 on a Saturday, call me. Don't wait for Monday.
listings.why: He picks up on Saturdays, which is when the bakeries need him.

listings.name: Tanglaw Career Coaching
listings.tagline: Resumes and interview practice for internationally trained pros
listings.serviceArea: Toronto. Video sessions anywhere in Ontario.
listings.story: Cristina Navarro was a nurse in Manila and a cashier in Toronto for her first two years, which she talks about openly. Now she runs mock interviews out of a co-working space at Yonge and Eglinton, mostly for nurses, engineers and accountants who are rebuilding a career here.
listings.quote: Your resume from home is not wrong. It's just written for a different reader.
listings.why: She's been through the same restart and doesn't sugarcoat it.

listings.name: Sining Web & Social
listings.tagline: Simple websites and social pages for small businesses
listings.story: Kevin Lopez builds one-page websites for restaurants and salons along The Queensway. He takes the photos himself, usually before opening, when the light is good and the owner hasn't started cooking yet.
listings.quote: Most of my clients don't need an app. They need their hours on Google to be right.
listings.why: He fixes your Google hours and photos first, before selling you anything bigger.

terms: Pilot Edition: Pinoy Pages 2026–2027 (Category: Money & Business, Greater Toronto Area). The printed proof copy is released spring (April 16, 2027); the website is updated year-round.
Prices are per issue: Free, or Verified $199 with everything included. No add-ons, bundles or founding discounts in the pilot. Ads return in the April 2027 edition.

Verified Kabayan badge: payment never buys the badge. Verified listings are only eligible; the badge is earned by four checks: a ~15-minute verification visit (kabayan-owned or run, really trading, ZCard completed) plus one mutual vouch from a verified business, confirmed by both. In the pilot, founding members are vouched for at the visit. We may withhold the badge if a check fails; the Verified listing continues without it.
Free listings are unverified: name and contact only, with no badge, no QR code, no Save contact button, no ZCard, and they can't give or receive vouches.
Keeping your badge — validity: the badge is valid for one edition (12 months from the verification date). A light re-check at renewal updates the “Verified [date]”.
Keeping your badge — vouch: at least one mutual vouch must stay active. If a vouch is removed, you have a 60-day grace period to replace it; after that the badge is paused.
Keeping your badge — current details: contact details and the ZCard must stay current. A dead phone number or a closed business pauses the badge.
Keeping your badge — renewal: if you don't renew, the badge is removed and the listing drops to a Free listing.
Keeping your badge — complaints: a complaint pauses the badge pending review. Paused badges are not shown.
QR codes always resolve through pinoypages.ca. Our pages never ask for a login, a payment or personal information.
Pilot price lock: advertisers who renew on time (paid by December 18 each year) keep their pilot tier price for the next edition.

Member renewal discount: existing paid members who renew by the on-time date (December 18) get a flat 20% off their locked price for the next edition (e.g. Verified $199 becomes $159). Existing members only; not available to new sign-ups; does not stack or compound; valid for one renewal year and reviewed each edition.
Late renewal: renewals after the on-time date are charged the current regular price and lose the price lock and member discount.
Website mirror: your online presence mirrors your print presence and is included free in every tier.
No guarantee of results: we report scan counts monthly (Verified). We do not promise any number of leads, calls, sales or visitors.

Printed edition: a short-run proof copy for advertisers (one copy per paid advertiser) and a sales brochure for prospects. It is not sold or handed out to the public. If it does not print, print ad fees are refunded.
Prices are in CAD, plus applicable HST. Draft terms, to be reviewed by a lawyer before launch.
